paragraphs.text: The Planes-hopping Era is a fan nickname for the story period spanning the 2003–2008 blocks, during which each block focused on a different plane. Unlike later arcs, this era lacked a grand overarching storyline connecting the planes; instead, each block told a self-contained narrative rooted in its own setting’s lore, which concluded before moving on to the next world. As a result, this period contains no formal saga or storyline arc following the end of the Mirari Saga .

Until then, the game’s narrative had revolved almost entirely around Dominaria , with only brief excursions into other planes such as Rabiah , Ulgrotha , Phyrexia , Serra's Realm , Rath , and Mercadia , most of which were presented in the context of how Dominarian planeswalkers influenced them. The Planes-hopping Era broke away from this Dominaria-centered focus, instead introducing a series of fresh worlds. Blocks during this time showcased Mirrodin , Kamigawa , Ravnica , Lorwyn , and Shadowmoor . It also marked a return to a post-apocalyptic Dominaria in the Time Spiral block, which acted as an epilogue for the Planeswalker Wars.
The Planes-hopping Era includes the Mirrodin Cycle , Kamigawa Cycle , Ravnica Cycle , Time Spiral Cycle , Lorwyn Cycle , and Shadowmoor Cycle .

While the pattern of shifting from plane to plane would continue well beyond this era, the storyline itself returned to a saga format starting with Alara Unbroken , which started followed individual planeswalkers across the planes and cycles — marking the beginning of the Planeswalker Saga .
